text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze fired Hungary's top four police officers on Friday citing economic mismanagement and a rising trend of corruption and the lack of progress in uncovering the recent crime wave in Budapest.

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs who is part of a Hungarian delegation headed by Prime Minister Gyula Horn to the Lisbon summit of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe said that the summint will also provide ample opportunity for bilateral meetings.
- Newly installed Romanian President Emil Constantinescu expressed thanks for Transylvanian votes which put him into the top executive office and called for the country to show unity and solidarity.
- The first congress of the opposition Hungarian Democratic People's Party Saturday reelected incumbent Ivan Szabo to the post of party president.

- The national board of the Socialists held a meeting on Saturday, establishing that the party continues to regard the trade unions as their strategic allies and is ready at the 1988 elections to renew its electoral alliance of 1994 with the largest union, the National Confederation of Hungarian Trade Unions.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. decided on the privatisation of the Savings Bank on Friday. 66 percent of the bank's HUF 1.3 billion registered capital will be offered for sale.
- Police captured two arms smugglers last Thursday, seizing 30 hand grenades, detonators, timing devices, explosives and armour piercing missiles.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Russian Defence Minister Igor Rogionov Friday warned Central European states seeking to join NATO that Russia may target them with nuclear missiles should they join the alliance. (Sat.)
- Parliament will again hold a three-day plenary session this week, closing debates on social care and the state news agency MTI, and winding up detailed debate of next year's budget. (Sat.)
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. is planning to offer 14 major companies for privatisation next year, including the national airlines Malev, the shipping company Mahart, the film producer and distributor Mafilm.
- A delegation from the IMF is expected to pay a fact-finding visit to Budapest Wednesday.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Organisers of a $350 million syndicated loan package granted to the National Bank in August have agreed to reduce the interest surcharge from the original 50 base points above LIBOR to 20 base points.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- A total of $1.146 billion in working capital was invested in the Hungarian economy in the first eight months of this year, 42 percent more than in the same period of last year.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Gasoline prices will go up by more than HUF 12 per litre from January due to an increase in VAT and contributions to the Road Fund. Telephone charges, Budapest public transport ticket and tobacco prices will also go up on January 1.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
